translations.text: The Book of the Revelation of Baruch son of Neriah. Translated from Greek into Syriac.
In the twenty-fifth year of Jeconiah king of Judah, the word of the Lord came to Baruch son of Neriah, and he said to him:
I have seen everything that this people has done to me. The evils committed by these two remaining tribes are greater than those of the ten tribes that were taken captive.
For the earlier tribes were compelled by their kings to sin, but these two tribes themselves pressured and compelled their kings to sin.

Therefore, look, I am bringing disaster upon this city and its inhabitants. It will be removed from my presence for a time. I will scatter this people among the nations, so that they may benefit the nations,
and my own people may be disciplined. A time will come when they will seek the prosperity of their times.
I have told you these things so that you may tell Jeremiah and all who are like you to withdraw from this city.
For your deeds are like a firm pillar for this city, and your prayers are like a strong wall.
And I said, “O Lord, my Lord, have I come into the world for this—to see my mother’s suffering? No, my Lord!”
If I have found mercy in your eyes, take my spirit first, so that I may go to my ancestors and not see the destruction of my mother.
For both things distress me greatly: I cannot stand against you, but neither can my soul bear to see my mother's suffering.
But there is one thing I would say before you, Lord.
What, then, will happen after these things? For if you destroy your city and hand your land over to enemies, how will the name of Israel be remembered again?
Or how will we speak of your praises? Or to whom will the things in your law be explained?
Or will the ordered creation return to its original state, and the world go back again to its ancient silence,
with the multitude of souls taken away and the human race no longer named?
And where is everything you said to Moses about us?
The Lord said to me: This city will be handed over for a time, and the people will be disciplined for a time, but the world will not be forgotten.
Or do you suppose that this is the city of which I said, 'I have inscribed you on the palms of my hands'?

The building now built among you is not the one revealed in my presence, the one prepared here beforehand, from the time when I resolved to make Paradise. I showed it to Adam before he sinned, but when he transgressed the commandment, it was taken away from him, as Paradise also was.
After these things, I showed it to my servant Abraham at night, between the divided pieces of the sacrifices.
I also showed it to Moses on Mount Sinai, when I showed him the pattern of the tabernacle and all its furnishings.
And now, look, it is kept in my presence, as Paradise also is.
Go, then, and do as I command you.

I answered and said: Am I, then, destined to be held accountable for Zion, when your enemies come to this place, defile your sanctuary, plunder your inheritance, and rule over those whom you have loved? They will then return to the land of their idols and boast before them. And what have you done for your great name?
The Lord said to me: My name and my glory endure forever, but my judgment reserves its rightful claim for its appointed time.
You will see with your own eyes that it is not the enemies who overthrow Zion or burn Jerusalem; rather, they serve the Judge for a time.
But you, go and do everything that I have told you.
I went and took Jeremiah, Iddo, Seraiah, Jabesh, Gedaliah, and all the dignitaries of the people, and brought them to the Kidron Valley. I told them everything that had been said to me.
They all raised their voices and wept.
We sat there and fasted until evening.
The next day, the Chaldean army surrounded the city. In the evening, I, Baruch, left the people and went out and stood by the oak tree.
I was grieving over Zion and sighing over the captivity that had come upon the people.
Suddenly, a mighty spirit lifted me up and carried me high above the wall of Jerusalem.
I looked and saw four angels standing at the four corners of the city, each holding a burning torch in his hands.
Another angel came down from heaven and said to them, “Hold your torches, and do not set anything on fire until I tell you.
For I have been sent first to speak a word to the earth and to place with it what the Lord Most High commanded me.”

I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies and take from there the curtain at the entrance, the holy ephod, the mercy seat, the two tablets, the sacred clothing of the priests, the censer, the forty-eight precious stones that the priest used to wear, and all the sacred utensils of the tabernacle.

He said to the earth in a loud voice, “Earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the mighty God! Receive these things that I entrust to you, and keep them until the last times, so that, when you are commanded, you may give them back, and foreigners may not gain possession of them.
For the time has come for Jerusalem also to be handed over for a time, until it is said that it is to be restored again forever.”
And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them.

After this, I heard that angel say to the angels who were holding the torches, “Now begin, and tear down its walls to their foundations, so that the enemies may not boast and say, ‘We have torn down Zion’s wall and burned the dwelling place of the mighty God.’”
And [?] took me to the place where I had stood before.
The angels did as he commanded them. When they had demolished the corners of the wall, after the wall had fallen, a voice was heard from inside the temple, saying:
“Enter, enemies, and come, you who hate us! For the one who guarded the house has abandoned it.”
Then I, Baruch, went away.
After this, the Chaldean army entered and seized the temple and everything around it.
They took the people captive and killed some of them. They bound King Zedekiah and sent him to the king of Babylon.
I, Baruch, came with Jeremiah, whose heart was found pure from sins and who had not been caught up in the turmoil of the city. We tore our clothes, wept, mourned, and fasted for seven days.
After seven days, the word of God came to me and said:
“Tell Jeremiah to go and escort the captive people as far as Babylon.
But you are to remain here among the ruins of Zion. After these days, I will show you what is to happen in the last days.”
I told Jeremiah as the Lord had commanded me.
He went with the people, but I, Baruch, returned and sat before the gates of the temple. I uttered this lament over Zion, saying:
Blessed is the one who was not born, or the one who was born and died.
“But as for us who are alive, woe to us, who see Zion’s troubles and what has happened to Jerusalem!”

I will call the sirens from the sea. And you, night demons, come from the desert, and you, demons and jackals, from the forests. Wake up and gird your waists for dancing. Take up lamentations with me and dance with me.
You farmers, do not sow again. And you, earth, why have you yielded the fruits of your harvests? Keep the sweetness of your food shut up within you.
And you, vine, why do you continue to yield your wine? For none of it is offered in Zion anymore, and firstfruits are no longer offered.
And you, heavens, withhold your dew, and do not open the storehouses of rain.
And you, sun, withhold the light of your rays. And you, moon, extinguish your abundant light. For why should light shine again where Zion’s light has grown dark?
And you, bridegrooms, do not enter. Let virgins not adorn themselves with crowns. And you women, do not pray to give birth.
For let barren women rejoice all the more, and let those who have no children be glad. Let those who have children be distressed.
For why should they give birth in pain and bury their children with groans?
Or why should human beings have children anymore? Or why should the offspring of their kind still be named, when this mother lies devastated and her children have been taken captive?
From now on, do not speak of beauty anymore, and do not talk about loveliness.

But you, priests, take the keys of the sanctuary and throw them to the heights of heaven. Give them to the Lord and say, “Guard your house yourself, for look, we have been found to be dishonest stewards.”

And you, virgins who spin fine linen and silk with gold from Ophir, hurry, take everything, and throw it into the fire, so that it may carry them to the one who made them, and the flame may send them to the one who created them, so that enemies will not gain possession of them.
But I, Baruch, say this against you, Babylon: If you had prospered while Zion dwelt in her glory, it would have caused us great pain that you had become Zion’s equal.
But now, look: there is pain without limit and groaning beyond measure, because you prosper while Zion lies devastated.
Who will judge these things? Or to whom shall we complain about what has happened to us? O Lord, how have you endured it?
Our ancestors died without pain, and the righteous now sleep peacefully in the earth.
For they did not know this distress, nor did they hear about what has happened to us.
Earth, may you have ears, and you, dust, a heart. Go and announce it in Sheol, and say to the dead:
You are more blessed than we who are alive.
But this is what I say as I reflect, and I speak against you, prosperous land:
The midday heat does not blaze forever, nor do the sun’s rays shine continually.
Do not assume and expect that you will always prosper and rejoice. Do not exalt yourself too greatly and oppress others.
For truly, in its time, wrath will rise against you—the wrath that is now held back by patience, as though by reins.
After I had said these things, I fasted for seven days.
After these things, I, Baruch, was standing on Mount Zion, and a voice came from on high and said to me:
Stand on your feet, Baruch, and hear the word of Almighty God.
Because you have been astonished at what has happened to Zion, you will indeed be preserved until the end of the ages, to serve as a witness.
For if the prosperous cities should ever say, ‘Why has Almighty God brought this punishment upon us?’
You and those like you, who have seen this calamity and the punishments coming upon you and your people, must tell them, at the time when the nations are thoroughly chastised.
And then they will remain.
And if they say at that time, “When?”
You shall say to them, “You who drank the clear wine, drink its dregs as well. For the judgment of the Most High shows no partiality.”
For this reason, he did not spare his own children first, but dealt harshly with them as with his enemies, because they sinned.
Then, therefore, they were disciplined so that they might be forgiven.
But now you peoples and nations are guilty, because all this time you have trampled the earth and used creation unjustly.
For I was always doing good to you, but you were always ungrateful.

And I answered and said, “Look, you have made known to me the course of the times and what is to happen after these things. And you have told me that the punishment you spoke of is coming upon the nations.”
And now I know that many have sinned, lived in prosperity, and departed from the world. But few nations will remain in those times—the ones to whom the words you spoke apply.
For what benefit is there in this? Or what worse things than these events we see happening are we waiting to see?
But I will speak before you again.

What did those who had knowledge in your presence gain, who did not follow emptiness like the rest of the nations and did not say to the dead, “Give us life,” but always feared you and did not abandon your ways?
Look, they exerted themselves, yet you did not have mercy on Zion even for their sake.
And if others acted wickedly, Zion ought to have been forgiven because of the deeds of those who did good, rather than drowned because of the deeds of those who practiced injustice.
But who, O Lord my Lord, can comprehend your judgment? Or who can investigate the depth of your way? Or who can reckon the weight of your path?
Or who can ponder your incomprehensible purpose? Or who among those ever born has found the beginning or the end of your wisdom?
For we have all become like a vapor.
For just as a vapor rises without conscious purpose and then vanishes again, so is human nature: people depart against their will, and they do not know what will happen to them in the end.
For the righteous await the end with good reason, and they depart from this dwelling without fear, because the worth of their deeds is kept with you in treasuries.
For this reason they too leave this world without fear, and with confidence and joy they wait to receive the world you promised them.
But woe to us, who are afflicted even now and expect calamities at that time!
But you know precisely what you have done through your servants, because we cannot understand what is good as you do, our Maker.
But I will speak before you again, O Lord my Lord.
Long ago, when the world and its inhabitants did not yet exist, you formed a purpose and spoke a word, and immediately the works of creation stood before you.
And you said that you would make a human being for your world as a steward of your works, so that it might be known that he was not made for the world, but the world for him.
And now I see that the world that was made for our sake still remains, while we, for whose sake it came into being, are passing away.
And the Lord answered and said to me, “You have rightly wondered about the departure of human beings, but you have not judged rightly concerning the calamities that befall those who sin.”
And as for your saying that the righteous were snatched away while the wicked prospered,
And as for your saying that no one knows your judgment,
listen, then, and I will tell you. Pay attention to me, and I will let you hear my words.
A human being would rightly have been ignorant of my judgment if he had not received the law and if I had not instructed him in understanding.
But now, because he transgressed knowingly, he will also be punished knowingly.
And as for the righteous, of whom you said that this world came into being for their sake—the world to come is also for their sake.
For this world is a contest and toil for them, with great weariness, but the world to come is a crown with great glory.
I answered and said, “Lord, my Lord, look: our present years are few and miserable. Who can inherit what is immeasurable in this short time?”
The Lord answered and said to me, “With the Most High, neither a long time nor a few years are taken into account.
For what did Adam gain by living nine hundred and thirty years, when he transgressed the command he had received?
The long time he lived did not benefit him. Instead, he brought death and cut short the years of those born from him.
Or what did Moses lose by living only one hundred and twenty years? Because he submitted to the one who formed him, he brought the law to Jacob’s descendants and lit a lamp for the people of Israel.”
I answered and said, “The one who lit it drew from the light, but few followed his example.
The many for whom he lit it drew from Adam’s darkness and did not enjoy the light of the lamp.”
He answered and said to me, “That is why he established a covenant for them at that time and said, ‘Look, I have set life and death before you,’ and called heaven and earth as witnesses against them.
For he knew that his time was short, but heaven and earth remain for all time.

Yet after his death they sinned and transgressed, knowing that they had a law to rebuke them, a light in which nothing could go astray, and also the stars as witnesses. And I judge everything that exists.
But do not brood over these things or be troubled about what has happened.
For now it is the end of time—or of affairs, or of prosperity, or of dishonor—that must be considered, and not its beginning.
For if someone prospers in his early years but suffers humiliation in his old age, he forgets all the prosperity he once had.
And again, if someone suffers humiliation in his early years but prospers in his later years, he no longer remembers his humiliation.

Listen further: throughout this whole time, from the day when death was decreed against those who pass through this age, if everyone prospered but was destroyed in the end, everything would have been in vain.
Therefore, look, days are coming when times will hasten more than the former ones, seasons will run faster than those that have passed, and years will pass more swiftly than the present ones.
That is why I have now removed Zion, so that I may hasten all the more and visit the world at its appointed time.
Now, then, hold in your heart everything I command you, and seal these things in the chambers of your mind.
Then I will show you the judgment of my power and my ways that cannot be fathomed.
Go, then, and sanctify yourself for seven days. Do not eat bread or drink water, and do not speak to anyone.
After this, come to this place, and I will reveal myself to you. I will speak true things with you and instruct you about the course of the times, for they are coming and will not be delayed.”

I went from there and stayed in the Kidron Valley, in a cave in the earth. I consecrated myself there. I ate no bread and did not grow hungry; I drank no water and did not grow thirsty. I remained there until the seventh day, as he had commanded me.
Afterward, I came to the place where he had spoken with me.
At sunset, my soul was filled with many thoughts, and I began to speak before the Mighty One. I said:

O you who made the earth, hear me—you who established the firmament by your word and made the heights of heaven firm by your spirit, who called from the beginning of the world to things that did not yet exist, and they obey you.
You commanded the air by a gesture, and you saw things to come as though they had already passed.

You directed the heavenly armies that stand before you with great wisdom. You also governed with fierceness the countless holy living creatures that you made long ago from flame and fire, which stand around your throne.
You alone have the power to do instantly whatever you wish.
You send down the raindrops upon the earth by number, and you alone know the completion of the ages before they arrive. Look upon my petition.
For you alone can sustain all who exist, those who have passed away and those who are to come, those who sin and those who act righteously, as the living one who cannot be fathomed.
For you alone are the living one who does not die and cannot be fathomed, and you know the number of human beings.
And although many have sinned over time, others have acted righteously to no small degree.
You know where the final destiny of those who have sinned is kept, and the end of those who have acted righteously.
For if everyone had only this life here, nothing would be more bitter than this.
For what good is strength that turns into sickness, or plentiful food that turns into hunger, or beauty that turns ugly?
For human nature is constantly changing.
Or nothing? For we are not now as we were formerly, and we will not remain afterward as we are now.
For if there were not to be a final outcome for everything, our beginning would have been in vain.
But make known to me everything that comes from you, and enlighten me about what I ask of you.
How long will what is corruptible endure? How long will the time of mortals flourish? Until when will those who pass through the world be polluted with great wickedness?
Command, then, in mercy, and bring about everything you said you would bring, so that your power may be known to those who think your patience is weakness.
Show those who do not know, but have seen what has happened to us and to our city until now, how patient your rule is, because you called us by your name, a beloved people.
Measure out, then, mortal nature from now on.

Rebuke the angel of death from now on. Let your glory be seen and the greatness of your majesty be known. Let Sheol be sealed so that from now on it receives no more dead, and let the storehouses release the souls imprisoned in them.
For many years have lain desolate since the days of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and of all those like them who sleep in the earth, for whose sake you said you created the world.
Now show your glory quickly, and do not delay what you have promised.
When I had finished the words of this prayer, I became very weak.
After these things, behold, the heavens were opened. I looked, and strength was given to me, and a voice was heard from the heights, saying to me:
Baruch, Baruch, why are you troubled?
Someone who travels along a road does not finish it. Or someone who sails on the sea—unless he reaches a harbor, can he find comfort?
Or someone who promises another person a gift but does not fulfill his promise—is that not fraud?
Or someone who sows a field but does not harvest its fruit in season—does he not ruin it all?
Or someone who plants a plant—unless it grows until its proper season, can the one who planted it expect to receive fruit from it?
Or a pregnant woman, if she gives birth before her time—does she not kill her child?
Or someone who builds a house—unless he roofs it and completes it, can it be called a house? First answer me these things.
And I answered and said, “No, Lord, my Lord.”
And he answered and said to me, “Why, then, are you troubled about something you do not know? And why are you impatient about something you do not understand?
For just as I have not forgotten human beings, those who remain and those who have passed away, so I remember those who are remembered and those who are coming.

For when Adam sinned and death was decreed against those who would be born, the total number of those who would be born was counted. And for that number a place was prepared where the living would dwell and where the dead would be kept.
Unless, therefore, the number previously spoken of is completed, creation will not live. For my spirit creates the living, and Sheol receives the dead.
And you must also hear what is to come after these times.
For truly my salvation is close to coming, and is not far away as it was before.

For look, the days are coming when the books will be opened in which the sins of all who have sinned are written, and also the treasuries in which the righteousness of all who have acted righteously in creation has been gathered.

And at that time you and many who are with you will see the patience of the Most High, how in every generation he was patient with all who were born, both those who sinned and those who acted righteously.”
And I answered and said, “But look, Lord, no one knows the number of those who have passed away or of those who are yet to come.
For even I know what has happened to me, but I do not know what will happen to our enemies, or when you will attend to your servants.”
And he answered and said to me, “You too will be kept until that time, for the sign that the Most High is going to perform for the inhabitants of the earth at the end of days.
This, then, will be the sign:
When bewilderment seizes the inhabitants of the earth, and they fall into many afflictions and also fall into great torments,
and when, because of their great affliction, they say in their thoughts, ‘The Mighty One no longer remembers the earth,’ then, when they give up hope, the time will awaken.”
And I answered and said, “Will that coming affliction last a long time? Will that distress continue for many years?”
And he answered and said to me, “That time has been divided into twelve parts, and each one is reserved for what has been appointed for it.
In the first part there will be the beginning of upheavals.
And in the second part, the killing of great rulers.
And in the third part, the fall of many in death.
And in the fourth part, the sending out of the sword.
And in the fifth part, famine and the withholding of rain.
And in the sixth part, earthquakes and anguish.
And in the eighth part, many apparitions and attacks by demons.
And in the ninth part, fire falling.
And in the tenth part, much plundering and oppression.
And in the eleventh part, injustice and shamelessness.
And in the twelfth part, the confusion of all the things mentioned above mixed together.
These parts of that time are reserved, and they will be mixed with one another and serve one another.

For some of them leave out some of what belongs to them and take from others, and some complete both what belongs to them and what belongs to others, so that those who are on earth will not understand in those days of the end of times.
But whoever understands then will become wise.
The measure and reckoning of that time will be two parts: weeks of seven weeks.
And I answered and said, “It would be good for a person to reach that time and see it. Yet better than this would be not to reach it, so as not to fall.
But I will also say this:
Will the one who is imperishable despise perishable things and whatever happens among these perishable things, so that he may look only to imperishable things?
But, my Lord, if these things you have already told me are truly going to come, and if I have found mercy in your eyes, make this known to me as well:
Are these things going to happen in one place or in one region of the earth, or will the whole earth feel them?”
And he answered and said to me, “What happens then will affect the whole earth. Therefore all who are alive will feel it.
But at that time I will protect only those who are found in this land in those days.
And after what is to happen in these divisions has been completed, then the Messiah will begin to be revealed.

And Behemoth will be revealed from his place, and Leviathan will come up from the sea, the two great monsters that I created on the fifth day of creation and kept until that time. Then they will become food for all who remain.

The earth too will yield its fruit ten-thousandfold. On one vine there will be a thousand branches, and one branch will produce a thousand clusters, and one cluster will produce a thousand grapes, and one grape will produce a kor of wine.
And those who have been hungry will enjoy themselves. Moreover, they will see wonders every day.
For winds will go out from before me to bring the fragrance of aromatic fruits every morning, and at the end of the day, clouds will sprinkle healing dew.
And at that time the storehouse of manna will again come down from above, and they will eat from it during those years, because they are the ones who have reached the end of time.
And after these things, when the time of the Messiah’s coming is fulfilled and he returns in glory, then all who have fallen asleep in hope of him will rise.

And at that time the storehouses in which the full number of the souls of the righteous has been kept will be opened, and they will come out. The multitude of souls will appear together in one assembly, of one mind. The first will rejoice, and the last will not be distressed.
For they know that the time has arrived of which it was said that it is the culmination of the ages.
But when the souls of the wicked see all these things, they will then waste away all the more.
For they know that their torment has arrived and their destruction has come.
After these things, I went to the people and said to them, “Gather all your elders to me, and I will speak to you.”
And they all gathered in the Kidron Valley.
I spoke and said to them, “Listen, Israel, and I will speak to you; and you, offspring of Jacob, pay attention, and I will instruct you.
Do not forget Zion, but remember Jerusalem’s sufferings.
For look, days are coming when everything that has existed will be taken away to destruction and will be as though it had never existed.
But if you prepare your hearts to sow in them the fruits of the law, it will protect you at that time when the Mighty One is about to shake all creation.
For after a short time, the building of Zion will be shaken, so that it may be built again.
But that building will not endure. After a time it will again be uprooted, and Zion will remain desolate for a time.
Afterward it must be renewed in glory, and it will be perfected forever.
Therefore we should not grieve so much over the disaster that has now come as over what is still to come.
But greater than both these afflictions is the struggle when the Mighty One is about to renew his creation.
Now do not approach me for a few days, and do not visit me until I come to you.”
When I had said all these words to them, I, Baruch, went on my way. When the people saw me leaving, they raised their voices and wailed, saying,
“Where are you going, Baruch, away from us? Are you abandoning us like a father who leaves his children orphaned and goes away from them?
Are these the instructions that your companion Jeremiah the prophet gave you when he said to you,
‘Look after this people while I go and make arrangements in Babylon for the rest of our brothers, against whom the sentence has been issued that they should be taken captive’?
And now, if you too abandon us, it would be better for us all to die first, and only then for you to leave us.”

I answered the people and said, “Far be it from me to abandon you or leave you. I am only going as far as the Holy of Holies to petition the Mighty One concerning you and Zion, to see whether I may receive any further enlightenment. After this I will return to you.”
And I, Baruch, went to the holy place, sat on its ruins, and wept and said,
“O my eyes, become springs, and my eyelids, a fountain of tears!
For how shall I lament over Zion, and how shall I mourn over Jerusalem?
For in this place where I now wallow, the high priest formerly offered holy offerings and placed fragrant incense made of sweet-smelling spices.
But now our pride has become dust, and the longing of our souls has become sand.
After I said these things, I lay down there and saw a vision in the night.
There was a forest of trees planted on a plain, surrounded by high mountains with rugged cliffs. That forest occupied a vast area.
And there, opposite it, a vine sprang up, and from beneath it a spring flowed gently.
The spring reached the forest and became great waves. These waves swept over the forest and suddenly uprooted the bulk of it, overthrowing all the mountains around it.
The height of the forest was brought low, and the mountain peaks were brought low. That spring became so powerful that it left nothing of that vast forest except a single cedar.

It also cast that cedar down, and destroyed and uprooted the bulk of the forest, so that nothing would remain of it and not even its location would be known. But the vine itself came along with the spring, quietly and very gently. It came to a place not far from the cedar, and the cedar, lying fallen, was brought near it.

I looked, and that vine opened its mouth and spoke to the cedar, saying, “Are you not the cedar that remained from the forest of wickedness? Through you wickedness continued to be done all these years, and never anything good.

You exercised power over what was not yours, and you never even had compassion on what was yours. You extended your dominion over those far from you, and you caught those who came near you in the traps of your wickedness. You always exalted yourself as though you could not be uprooted.
But now your time has hastened, and your hour has arrived.”

Go, then, you too, cedar, after the forest that went before you. Become dust with it, and let your dust mingle together. Sleep now in distress and rest in torment until your final time comes, when you will return again and be tormented still more.
After this I saw that cedar burning and the vine growing. Everything around it became a plain full of flowers that do not wither. Then I awoke and got up.
I prayed and said, “Lord, my Lord, you always give light to those who conduct themselves with understanding.
Your law is life, and your wisdom is uprightness.
Make known to me, then, the interpretation of this vision.
For you know that my soul has always occupied itself with your law, and throughout my days I have not strayed from your wisdom.”
And he answered and said to me, “Baruch, this is the interpretation of the vision you saw.”
“As for the vast forest you saw, surrounded by high and rugged mountains, this is its meaning:
Look, the days are coming when this kingdom, which once destroyed Zion, will be destroyed and subjected to the one that comes after it.
That kingdom too will be destroyed after a time, and another, a third, will arise. It too will exercise power in its time and be destroyed.

After these, a fourth kingdom will arise, whose dominion will be harsh and more wicked than those that came before it. It will rule for many ages, like the forests of the plain, and hold power for a time. It will rise higher than the cedars of Lebanon.
Truth will be hidden within it, and all those entangled in wickedness will flee to it, as wild beasts flee and hide in a forest.

And when the time approaches for it to come to its end and fall, then the dominion of my Messiah will be revealed, which is like the spring and the vine. When it is revealed, it will uproot the multitude of its army.
As for the cedar you saw lying fallen, which remained from that forest, and the words you heard the vine speak to it, this is their meaning:

The last ruler will then remain alive when the multitude of his forces is destroyed. He will be bound, and they will bring him up to Mount Zion. My Messiah will rebuke him for all his wicked deeds, and will gather and set before him all the deeds of his forces.
Afterward he will kill him and shelter the remnant of my people who are found in the place I have chosen.
His rule will stand forever, until the world of corruption comes to an end and the times foretold are fulfilled.
This is your vision, and this is its interpretation.”
I answered and said, “For whom, and for how many, will these things happen? And who will be worthy to live at that time?”
I will speak before you about everything I am thinking, and I will ask you about the things I am pondering.
For look, I see many of your people who have departed from your covenants and thrown off the yoke of your law.
But I have also seen others who have abandoned their empty ways and fled beneath your wings.
What, then, will happen to these people? Or how will that final age receive them?
Or will their time be weighed in a balance, and will they be judged according to the way the balance tips?
He answered and said to me, “I will show you these things too.
For you asked to whom these things would happen, and to how many. Those who have believed will receive the good spoken of earlier, while those who treat it with contempt will receive the opposite.
As for what you said about those who have drawn near and those who have departed, this is the answer:
Those who submitted at first, but afterward departed and mingled with the offspring of the mixed nations—their earlier time is counted as dung.
And those who at first did not know, but afterward came to know life and mingled with the offspring of the chosen people—their earlier time is counted as dung.
Times succeed times, and seasons succeed seasons, each taking over from another. Then, at the end, everything will be compared according to the measure of the times and the hours of the seasons.
For destruction takes those who belong to it, and life takes those who belong to it.
The dust will be summoned and told, ‘Return what does not belong to you, and raise up everything you have kept until its appointed time.’
But you, Baruch, prepare your heart for what has been said to you, and understand what has been shown to you, for many everlasting consolations await you.

For you have gone from this place, and you are passing from the regions that are now visible to you. You have forgotten what is perishable, and you no longer remember the things that exist among mortals.
Go, then, instruct your people, and come to this place. Afterward, fast for seven days. Then I will come to you and speak with you.”
Then I, Baruch, went away from there and came to my people. I called my firstborn son, Gedaliah my friend, and seven of the elders of the people, and said to them:
“Look, I am going to my ancestors, as everyone on earth must go.
But you must not depart from the way of the law. Instead, watch over and warn the people who remain, so that they do not depart from the commandments of the Mighty One.
For you see that the one we serve is righteous, and our Maker shows no partiality.
Look at what has happened to Zion and what has befallen Jerusalem,
so that the judgment of the Mighty One may be known, and his ways, which are beyond searching out and are upright.
For if you endure and remain steadfast in reverence for him, and do not forget his law, the times will change for your good, and you will see Zion’s consolation.
For what is happening now is nothing, but what is yet to happen is very great.
For everything corruptible passes away, and everything that dies departs. This whole present age will be forgotten, and there will be no remembrance of this present age, which is mingled with evils.
For whoever runs now runs toward emptiness, and whoever prospers will soon fall and be brought low.
For what is to come is what should be sought, and what comes afterward is what we hope for. For there is an age that does not pass away.

And that time which lasts forever is coming, and the new world, which does not turn those who enter it at its beginning back to corruption, nor show mercy to those who go to torment, nor lead those who live in it to destruction.
For these are the ones who will inherit this time that has been spoken of, and theirs is the inheritance of the promised time.
These are the ones who have stored up treasures of wisdom for themselves, and with whom stores of understanding have been found, who have not departed from mercy and have kept the truth of the law.
For the world to come is given to these, but the dwelling of the rest of the multitude will be in fire.
Therefore, instruct the people as much as you can, for this labor is ours.
For if you teach them, you will give them life.
And my son and the elders of the people answered and said to me, “Has the Mighty One brought us so low that he will take you from us so soon?
We will certainly be in darkness, and there will be no light for the people who remain.
For where will we seek the law again? Or who will distinguish for us between death and life?”
And I said to them, “I cannot stand against the throne of the Mighty One. Nevertheless, Israel will not lack a wise man, nor the descendants of Jacob someone versed in the law.
Only prepare your hearts to listen to the law, and submit to those who are wise and understanding in the fear of God. And prepare yourselves not to be separated from them.
For if you do these things, the good news I told you about before will come to you, and you will not fall into the torment about which I warned you before.”
But concerning my being taken away, I did not tell them, not even my son.
And when I had gone out and dismissed them, I went away from there and said to them, “Look, I am going to Hebron, for the Mighty One has sent me there.”
And I came to that place where he had spoken with me, and I stayed there and fasted for seven days.
And after the seventh day, I prayed before the Mighty One and said:

“O Lord, you summon the coming of the times, and they stand before you. You bring the dominion of the ages to an end, and they do not resist you. You govern the course of the seasons, and they obey you.
You alone know the span of the generations, and you do not reveal your mysteries to the many.
You make known the abundance of fire, and you have weighed the lightness of the wind.
You examine the farthest reaches of the heights, and you search the depths of darkness.
You command the number of those who have passed away, and it is preserved; and you have prepared a dwelling place for those who are yet to come.
You remember the beginning you made, and you do not forget the destruction that is to come.
With fearsome and furious gestures you command the flames, and they change into winds. By a word you bring into being what did not exist, and with great power you hold what has not yet come.
You have taught created things through your understanding, and you give wisdom to the constellations so that they serve in their appointed orders.
Countless hosts stand before you and serve peacefully in their appointed orders at your command.
Hear your servant and listen to my plea.
For we are born in a short time, and in a short time we return.
But to you, hours are like eras, and days like generations.
Therefore, do not be angry with human beings, for they are nothing, and do not hold our deeds against us.
For what are we? Through your gift we have come into the world, and we leave it against our will.
For we did not tell our fathers to beget us, nor did we send to Sheol and say, “Receive us.”
What strength do we have, then, to bear your anger? Or what are we, that we can endure your judgment?
Shelter us in your mercy, and help us in your compassion.
Look upon the lowly who have submitted to you, and save all who draw near to you. Do not cut off the hope of our people, and do not cut short the times of our help.
For this is the people you have chosen, and these are the people whose like you have not found.
But now I will speak before you and say what my heart thinks.
We trust in you, for your law is with us, and we know that we will not fall as long as we hold firmly to your covenants.
We are blessed at all times, even if only in this: that we have not mingled with the nations.
For we are all one renowned people, who have received one law from one. That law among us helps us, and the excellent wisdom within us will support us.
When I had prayed and said these things, I became very weak.
He answered and said to me, “You have prayed sincerely, Baruch, and all your words have been heard.
But my judgment demands its own, and my law demands what is due to it.
For I will answer you from your own words, and speak with you from your own prayer.
For this is precisely the point: the person who perishes is nothing, yet he acted wickedly as though he could accomplish something. He did not remember my goodness or accept my patience.
Therefore, you will certainly be taken away, as I told you before, and the time of which I told you is coming.
And that time of distress will arise. For it will come and pass with a fierce rush, and it will be turbulent as it comes in furious anger.
In those days, all the inhabitants of the earth will rest peacefully with one another, because they do not know that my judgment has drawn near.
For not many wise people will be found at that time, and those with understanding will be few. Even those who know will remain all the more silent.
There will be many rumors and no small amount of news. Acts of illusion will be displayed, and many promises will be recounted. Some will be empty, and some will be fulfilled.
Honor will turn to disgrace, strength will be brought low into contempt, order will break down, and beauty will become an object of scorn.
At that time, many will say to many others, “Where has the abundance of understanding hidden itself, and where has the abundance of wisdom gone?”

While they are thinking these things, jealousy will flare up in those of whom it was not expected, and passion will seize the one who was at peace. Many will be stirred to anger to injure many others, and they will rouse armies to shed blood. In the end, they will perish together with them.

And at that time the change of the times will become plainly visible to everyone, because throughout all these times they defiled themselves and acted unjustly. Each went about his own deeds, and they did not remember the law of the Mighty One.
Therefore fire will consume their thoughts, and the reflections of their innermost being will be tested in the flame. For the Judge will come and will not delay.
For every one of the earth’s inhabitants knew when he was doing wrong, yet because of their arrogance they did not acknowledge my law.
Then many will truly weep, but more for the living than for the dead.
And I answered and said, “Oh, Adam, what have you done to all those born from you? And what will be said to the first Eve, who listened to the serpent?
For this whole multitude has gone to destruction, and those whom the fire consumes cannot be counted.
But I will speak before you again.
You, Lord, my Lord, know what is in your creation.

For long ago you commanded the dust to bring forth Adam, and you know the number of those born from him, and how greatly those who came into being sinned before you and did not acknowledge you, their Maker.
For all these things their end reproves them, and your law, which they transgressed, repays them on your day.
But now let us leave the wicked and inquire about the righteous.
I will recount their blessedness and will not be silent in praising the glory reserved for them.
For truly, just as you endured great hardship for a short time in this passing world in which you live, so you will receive great light in that world which has no end.”
“But again I will ask you, Mighty One, and seek mercy from the one who made everything.
In what form will those who live in your day live? Or how will their splendor remain afterward?

Will they then take on this present form and be clothed in these limbs bound by sinews, which are now subject to evils and through which evils are committed? Or will you change those who were in the world, just as you change the world?”
And he answered and said to me, “Listen to this word, Baruch, and write everything you learn in the memory of your heart.

For the earth will certainly then return the dead whom it now receives to keep, changing nothing in their form. As it received them, so it will return them; and as I delivered them to it, so it will also raise them.
For then it will be necessary to show the living that the dead have come to life and that those who departed have returned.
And when those who now know one another have recognized one another, then judgment will take effect, and the things spoken of beforehand will come.
And after that appointed day has passed, the appearance of those who are condemned will be changed, as will the glory of those who are declared righteous.
For the appearance of those who now act wickedly will be made worse than it is, so that they may suffer torment.

As for the glory of those who have now been justified by my law, who had understanding during their lives and planted the root of wisdom in their hearts, their splendor will then be glorified through transformations. The appearance of their faces will be changed into the light of their beauty, so that they may obtain and receive the world that does not die, which is then promised to them.
For those who come then will groan all the more because they rejected my law and stopped their ears so as not to hear wisdom or receive understanding.

So when they see those over whom they now exalt themselves then exalted and glorified above them, both groups will be transformed: these into the splendor of angels, and those into startling sights and the spectacle of dreadful forms; and they will waste away still more.
For first they will see, and afterward they will go away to be tormented.
But those who have been saved through their deeds, and those for whom the law has now been hope, understanding an expectation, and wisdom faith, will see wonders in their proper times.
For they will see that world which is not visible to them now, and they will see the time that is now hidden from them.
And time will no longer make them grow old.

For they will dwell in the heights of that world, resembling angels and becoming like stars. They will be transformed into whatever form they wish, from beauty to loveliness, and from light to the radiance of glory.

For the expanses of Paradise will spread out before them, and they will be shown the beauty of the majesty of the living creatures beneath the throne, and all the hosts of angels who are now restrained by my word from being seen, and held by a command to remain in their places until their coming arrives.
Then the excellence of the righteous will be greater than that of the angels.
For the first will welcome the last, those for whom they had been waiting, and the last will welcome those whom they had heard had passed away.
For they have escaped this world of distress and laid down their burden of troubles.
For what, then, have human beings lost their lives, and for what have those who were on earth exchanged their souls?

For then they chose for themselves this time, which cannot pass without troubles. They chose for themselves that time whose outcomes are full of sighs and evils. They rejected the world that does not make those who come to it grow old, and despised the time and the glory, so that they will not come to the honor I spoke to you about before.
And I answered and said, “How mistaken are those for whom woe is then reserved!
Why, then, do we still mourn for those who die, or why do we weep for those who go to Sheol?
Let lamentations be reserved for the beginning of that torment which is to come, and let tears be set aside for the coming of the destruction that will occur then.
But even in the face of these things I will speak:
What should the righteous do now?
Take pleasure in the suffering you now endure. For why do you look to the downfall of your enemies?
Prepare yourselves for what is reserved for you, and make your souls ready for the reward laid up for you.”
And when I had said these things, I fell asleep there.

And I saw a vision: a cloud was rising from the very great sea. As I watched it, I saw that it was full of white and black waters. There were many colors in these waters, and something resembling a great lightning bolt appeared at the top of the cloud.
And I saw that cloud moving swiftly, racing along, and it covered the whole earth.
After this, that cloud began to rain down upon the earth the waters that were in it.
And I saw that the waters coming down from it were not all alike in appearance.

For at the very beginning they were very dark for a time. Afterward I saw that the waters were bright, but they were not abundant. After these I again saw dark waters, and after these bright waters again, then dark waters again, then bright waters again.
This happened twelve times, but the black waters were always more abundant than the bright ones.

And at the end of the cloud, it rained down black waters, darker than all the waters that had come before. Fire was mixed with them, and wherever those waters fell, they brought devastation and destruction.
After this I saw the lightning bolt that I had seen at the top of the cloud seize it and bring it down to the earth.
That lightning bolt shone exceedingly brightly, illuminating the whole earth, and healed those places where the last waters had fallen and caused devastation.
And he held the whole earth and gained dominion over it.
And after these things I saw, and behold, twelve streams were rising from the sea. They surrounded that lightning and were subject to it.
And I awoke in terror.

And I pleaded with the Mighty One and said, “You alone, Lord, know beforehand the heights of the world. By your word you bring about whatever happens in the course of time. In response to the deeds of the earth’s inhabitants, you hasten the beginnings of the times. You alone know the end of the ages.
Nothing is difficult for you, but you do everything easily with a gesture.
The depths, like the heights, come before you, and the beginnings of the ages serve your word.
You reveal to those who fear you what awaits them, so that they may be comforted from now on.

You make mighty deeds known to those who do not know. You break through the barrier for those who do not understand. You illuminate the darkness and reveal hidden things to those who are blameless, who have faithfully submitted to your entire law.
You have shown your servant this vision. Reveal its interpretation to me as well.

For I know that I have received an answer about the things I asked you, and you have revealed to me what I sought. And you have made known to me with what voice I should praise you, or with which parts of my body I should offer you praise and thanksgiving.

For even if the parts of my body became mouths and instruments of song, I would still be unable to repay you with praise or praise you as you deserve. Nor could I recount your praise or describe the splendor of your majesty.
For what am I among human beings? Or how am I regarded among those greater than I, that I have heard all these wonders from the Most High, and boundless promises from the one who created me?
Blessed is my mother among those who give birth, and praised among women shall be the one who bore me.
But I will not stop praising the Mighty One. Instead, with a voice of praise I will recount his wonders.
For who can match your wonders, God? Or who can comprehend your profound purpose concerning life?
For by your purpose you govern all the creatures your right hand created. You have established every fountain of light beside you, and you have prepared the treasuries of wisdom beneath your throne.
And those who did not love your law perish justly, and the torment of judgment awaits those who did not submit to your dominion.

For although Adam sinned first and brought death upon everyone before its time, each of those born from him has also prepared future punishment for himself, and each has also chosen for himself the glories to come.
For truly, the one who believes receives a reward.
But now, turn toward destruction, you wicked people of the present, for you are swiftly being called to account, because in your time you rejected the understanding of the Most High.
For his works did not teach you, nor did the craftsmanship continually displayed in his creation persuade you.
Therefore Adam is responsible only for himself, while each one of us has become Adam for himself.
But you, Lord, explain to me the things you have revealed to me, and make known to me what I have asked of you.
For at the end of the world, those who have acted wickedly will be called to account according to their wickedness, and you will glorify the faithful according to their faithfulness.
For you guide those who belong to you, and you erase those who sin from among your own.”
And when I had finished speaking the words of this prayer, I sat there beneath the tree to rest in the shade of its branches.

I marveled and was astonished, reflecting in my thoughts on the abundant goodness that the sinners on earth had pushed away from themselves, and on the great torment they had scorned, although they knew that they would be tormented because they had sinned.
While I was thinking about these things and others like them, Ramiel, the angel who presides over true visions, was sent to me and said to me:
“Why is your heart troubled, Baruch, and why are your thoughts disturbing you?
For if you have been so shaken merely by hearing about the judgment, what will happen when you see it openly with your own eyes?
And if you have become so undone through your expectation of the Mighty One’s day, what will happen when you reach its coming?
And if you have been so terrified at the report of the torment of those who have sinned, how much more so when the actual event reveals wonders?

And if you have heard the names of the good and evil things that are coming then and have become distressed, what will happen when you see what the Majesty reveals, rebuking some and bringing delight to others?
But because you asked the Most High to reveal to you the interpretation of the vision you saw, I have been sent to tell you.

The Mighty One has indeed made known to you the events of the times that have passed and those that are yet to pass in his world, from the beginning of his creation until its end—those involving deceit and those involving truth.
For the great cloud that you saw rising from the sea and moving to cover the earth is the span of the world that the Mighty One made when he planned to make the world.
And when the word went out from his presence, the span of the world stood as something small, and it was arranged according to the vast understanding of the one who sent it.
And the black waters that you saw first at the top of the cloud, which came down first upon the earth, are the transgression committed by Adam, the first human being.

For when he transgressed, untimely death came into being, mourning was named, distress was prepared, pain was created, toil was established, pride began to arise, and Sheol demanded to be renewed with blood. The conception of children came about, the passion of parents arose, the greatness of humanity was brought low, and goodness withered.
What, then, could have been blacker or darker than these things?
This is the beginning of the black waters that you saw.
And from these black waters, more black waters were born, and utter darkness came into being.
For he became a danger to himself, and he also became a danger to the angels.
For at that time when he was created, they had freedom.
And some of them came down and joined themselves to women.
Then those who had acted in this way were tormented in chains.
But the rest of the countless multitude of angels held themselves back.
And those who lived on the earth perished together through the waters of the flood.
These are the first black waters.
And after these, you saw bright waters. This is the spring of Abraham, together with his descendants and the coming of his son and his grandson and those who were like them.

For at that time the law was spoken of among them without being written down, and the deeds required by the commandments were being carried out. Faith in the coming judgment was then being born, hope for the world to be renewed was being built, and the promise of the life that comes afterward was being planted.
These are the bright waters that you saw.”

And the third waters, the black ones that you saw, are the mingling of all the sins that the nations committed afterward, after the death of those righteous people, and the wickedness of the land of Egypt, whose people acted wickedly by enslaving the children of those righteous people.
Yet they too perished in the end.
And the fourth waters, the bright ones that you saw, are the coming of Moses, Aaron, Miriam, Joshua son of Nun, Caleb, and all those who were like them.

For at that time the lamp of the eternal law shone upon all those who were sitting in darkness, to make known to those who believe the promise of their reward, and to those who deny it the torment of fire reserved for them.
But at that time even the heavens were wrenched from their place, and those beneath the throne of the Mighty One were shaken, when he took Moses to himself.

For he showed him many warnings, together with the requirements of the laws and the end of time, just as he showed you. He also showed him the likeness of Zion and the dimensions according to which it would be built, and the likeness of the present sanctuary.
But even then he showed him the dimensions of the fire, the depths of the abyss, the weight of the winds, and the number of the raindrops;
and the restraint of wrath, the abundance of patience, and the certainty of judgment;
and the root of wisdom, the wealth of understanding, and the fountain of knowledge;
and the height of the air, the greatness of Paradise, the end of the ages, and the beginning of the day of judgment;
and the number of the offerings, and the lands that have not yet come into being;
and the mouth of Gehenna, the place of vengeance, the region of faith, and the place of hope;

and the likeness of the torment to come, the multitude of angels beyond number, the armies of flame, the brilliance of the lightning, the sound of thunder, the ranks of the archangels, the treasuries of light, the changes of the times, and the intricacies of the law.
These are the fourth waters, the bright ones that you saw.

And the fifth waters, the black ones that you saw raining down, are the deeds that the Amorites performed, the incantations of the sorceries they practiced, the wickedness of their mysteries, and the mingling of their impurities.
But Israel too was defiled by sins at that time, in the days of the judges, although they saw the many signs performed by the one who made them.
And the sixth waters, the bright ones that you saw, are the time in which David and Solomon were born.
At that time Zion was built and the sanctuary was renewed. Much blood was shed among the nations that sinned then, and many offerings were presented at the renewal of the sanctuary.
And peace and tranquility prevailed at that time.
Wisdom was heard in the congregation, and the wealth of understanding increased in the assemblies.
The holy festivals were celebrated with goodness and great delight.
The judgment of the rulers was then seen to be without deceit, and the righteous requirements of the Mighty One's commandments were faithfully fulfilled.
And the land that was loved at that time was praised above all other lands because its inhabitants did not sin. The city of Zion then ruled over all lands and regions.
These are the bright waters that you saw.
And the seventh waters, the black ones that you saw, are the perversion of Jeroboam's thinking, when he planned to make two golden calves.
And all the wicked deeds committed by the kings who came after him.
And the curse of Jezebel, and the worship of idols that Israel practiced at that time.
And the withholding of rain and the famines that occurred, until women ate the fruit of their wombs.
And the time of their captivity, which came upon the nine and a half tribes because they were steeped in many sins.
And Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, came and took them captive.
But concerning the nations, there is much to say about how they continually acted unjustly and wickedly and never became righteous.
These are the seventh waters, the black ones that you saw.
And the eighth waters, the bright ones that you saw, are the righteousness and uprightness of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and the favor that came upon him.
For Sennacherib was stirred up to perish, and his anger was agitating him toward his destruction. And also the multitude of nations that were with him.

But when King Hezekiah heard what the Assyrian king was planning—to come and capture him and destroy his people, the two and a half tribes that remained, and that he also wanted to overthrow Zion—then Hezekiah trusted in his deeds and placed his hope in his righteousness. He spoke with the Mighty One and said:
“See, Sennacherib is preparing to destroy us, and he will boast and exalt himself when he has destroyed Zion.”
And the Mighty One heard him, for Hezekiah was wise, and he looked upon his petition because he was righteous.
Then the Mighty One commanded Ramiel, his angel who is speaking with you.
And I went out and destroyed their multitude. The number of their commanders alone was one hundred and eighty-five thousand, and each one of them had the same number under him.

At that time I burned their bodies from within, but I preserved their clothing and weapons on the outside, so that the wonders of the Mighty One might be seen all the more, and so that his name might be spoken of throughout the earth.
Zion was redeemed, and Jerusalem was rescued. Israel too was freed from its afflictions.
And all who were in the holy land rejoiced, and the name of the Mighty One was glorified so that it would be spoken of.
These are the bright waters that you saw.
And the ninth waters, the black ones that you saw, are all the wickedness that occurred in the days of Manasseh son of Hezekiah.

For he acted very wickedly: he killed the righteous, perverted justice, shed innocent blood, forcibly defiled married women, demolished altars and abolished their offerings, and expelled the priests so that they could not serve in the sanctuary.
And he made an image with five faces. Four of them faced the four directions, and the fifth was on top of the image, in defiance of the jealousy of the Mighty One.
Then wrath went out from the Mighty One so that Zion would be uprooted, just as has happened in your days.
And a sentence also went out against the two and a half tribes, that they too should be taken captive, as you have now seen.
And Manasseh's wickedness increased to such an extent that the glory of the Most High departed from the sanctuary.
For this reason Manasseh was called wicked at that time, and in the end his dwelling was in fire.
For when his petition to the Most High was heard, at the end, when he fell into the bronze horse and the bronze horse melted, it became a sign to him at that moment.
For he did not live perfectly, since he was not worthy. Rather, it was so that from then on he would know by whom he would have to be tormented in the end.
For the one who can do good can also torment.
Thus Manasseh acted wickedly, thinking in his time as though the Mighty One would not call him to account for these things.
These are the ninth waters, the black ones that you saw.

As for the tenth waters, the bright ones that you saw, these are the purity of the generation of Josiah, king of Judah. For at that time he alone submitted to the Mighty One with all his heart and all his soul.

He cleansed the land of idols and consecrated all the vessels that had been defiled. He restored the offerings to the altar, raised the horn of the faithful, exalted the righteous, and honored all who were wise in understanding. He restored the priests to their service and wiped out and removed magicians, sorcerers, and mediums from the land.
He not only killed the wicked who were alive, but they also brought the bones of those who had died out of their tombs and burned them in the fire.

He established the festivals and Sabbaths in their holiness and burned the defiled in the fire. He also burned in the fire the false prophets who had been leading the people astray. As for the people who had listened to them, he threw them alive into the Kidron Valley and heaped stones over them.
He was zealous for the Mighty One with all his soul. At that time he alone stood firm in the law, so that throughout his life he left no one uncircumcised or acting wickedly anywhere in the land.
He is the one who received an everlasting reward, and in the last time he will be honored before the Mighty One more than many others.
For his sake and for the sake of those like him, the glorious honors spoken of to you earlier were created and prepared.
These are the bright waters that you saw.
As for the eleventh waters, the black ones that you saw, these are the calamity now happening to Zion.

Or did you think that the angels feel no distress before the Mighty One because Zion has been handed over in this way? Look, the nations boast in their hearts, and crowds boast before their idols, saying, “She who trampled others for so long has been trampled, and she who enslaved others has been enslaved.”
Did you think that the Most High rejoices in these things, or that his name is glorified?
But what will become of his righteous judgment?
But after these things, those who have been scattered among the nations will be gripped by distress, and they will live in disgrace everywhere.

For as long as Zion is handed over and Jerusalem lies in ruins, the idols flourish in the cities of the nations, and the fragrance of the smoke of the incense of righteousness prescribed by the law has ceased in Zion, while everywhere in Zion's place there is now the smoke of wickedness.
But the king of Babylon, who has now overthrown Zion, will rise up and boast over the people, and in his heart he will speak arrogantly before the Most High.
Yet he too will fall in the end.
These are the black waters.
As for the twelfth waters, the bright ones that you saw, this is their meaning.
For a time will come after these things when your people will fall into distress, so that they will be in danger of all perishing together.
Nevertheless, they will be delivered, and their enemies will fall before them.
And for a time they will enjoy great happiness.
And at that time, after a little while, Zion will be rebuilt, and its offerings will again be established. The priests will return to their service, and the nations will again come to glorify it.
Yet not as fully as at first.
But after these things, there will be a downfall of many nations.
These are the bright waters that you saw.
For the last waters you saw, which were darker than all those before them—the ones that came after the twelve and were gathered together—belong to the whole world.
For the Most High made the division beforehand, because he alone knows what is going to happen.
For, concerning the evils of the wicked who were to come before him, he foresaw their conduct [?].
And he foresaw the good works of the righteous that would be accomplished before him, and their conduct [?], apart from the things he is going to do at the end of the world.
For this reason, neither black waters are with black waters, nor bright waters with bright waters, for this is the end.
Listen, then, to the interpretation of these last black waters that are to come after the black waters. This is what they mean.

Look, days are coming, and when the world's time has ripened and the harvest of its seeds, both evil and good, arrives, the Mighty One will bring confusion of spirit and bewilderment of heart upon the earth, its inhabitants, and its rulers.
They will hate one another and provoke one another to war. The dishonored will rule over the honored, and the lowly will be exalted over the renowned.
The many will be handed over to the few, and those who were nothing will rule over the strong. The poor will become richer than the wealthy, and the wicked will be raised above the mighty.
The wise will be silent, and fools will speak. Then human plans will not stand, nor will the counsel of the powerful. The hope of those who hope will not be fulfilled.
When these things already spoken of take place, confusion will fall upon all humanity. Some will fall in battle, some will perish in afflictions, and some will be hindered by their own people.
The Most High will reveal those nations that he prepared beforehand, and they will come and wage war against the rulers who remain at that time.
Everyone who escapes the war will die in an earthquake. Whoever escapes the earthquake will burn in fire, and whoever escapes the fire will perish from famine.
Everyone who escapes and flees from all the things already spoken of, both those who conquered and those who were conquered, will be handed over into the hands of my servant, the Messiah.
For the whole earth will devour its inhabitants.
But the holy land will have mercy on its own people and will protect its inhabitants at that time.
This is the vision that you saw, and this is its interpretation.
I have come to tell you these things because your petition has been heard by the Most High.
Listen also concerning the bright waters that are to come at the end, after these black waters. This is what they mean.

After the signs that were foretold to you have come, when the nations are thrown into turmoil and the time of my Messiah arrives, he will summon all the nations. Some of them he will keep alive, and some he will kill.
These things, then, will come upon the nations that are to survive it.
Every nation that has not known Israel and has not trampled Jacob's descendants will live.
This is so that those from every nation may be subject to your people.
But all those who ruled over you or knew you—all these will be handed over to the sword.
And after he has humbled everything in the world and sits in peace forever on the throne of his kingdom, then he will be revealed in delight, and rest will appear.
Then healing will descend in dew, and disease will be driven away. Worry, distress, and sighing will pass away from humanity, and joy will spread throughout the earth.
And no one will again die before his time, nor will any adversity occur suddenly.
Lawsuits, accusations, disputes, acts of vengeance, bloodshed, desires, envy, hatred, and everything like them will be removed and go away to condemnation.
For these are the evils that have filled this world, and because of them human life has been greatly disturbed.
Wild animals will come from the forest and serve human beings. Asps and dragons will come out of their holes to submit to a child.
Then women will no longer have pain when they give birth, nor will they suffer when they bring forth the fruit of the womb.
In those days, reapers will not grow weary, nor will builders toil. For the work will proceed of itself, together with those doing it, with great ease.
For that time is the end of what is corruptible and the beginning of what is incorruptible.
For this reason, the things spoken of earlier will happen in it. For this reason, it is far from evils and close to the things that do not die.
These are the final bright waters that came after the final black waters.
And I answered and said, “Who can equal you in your goodness, my Lord? For it cannot be comprehended.
Or who can fathom your mercies, which have no limit?
Or who can comprehend your understanding?
Or who can recount the thoughts of your mind?
Or who among those born can hope to attain these things, except someone on whom you have mercy and compassion?
For unless you have mercy on human beings, those beneath your right hand cannot attain these things, except those who can be called by name in the numbered ranks.
But we who are alive, if we know why we have come and submit to the one who brought us out of Egypt, return to remembering the things that have passed and rejoice over what has happened.

But if we do not now know why we have come, and do not acknowledge the sovereignty of the one who brought us up from Egypt, we return to seeking the things that have now happened, and we are distressed with pain over what has occurred.”

And he answered and said to me, “Since the revelation of this vision has been explained to you as you prayed, hear the word of the Most High, so that you may know what will happen to you after these things.
For you will certainly depart from this earth, yet not to death, but to be kept until the appointed times.

Therefore go up to the summit of this mountain. All the regions of this earth will pass before you, along with the form of the inhabited world, the mountain peaks, the depth of the valley, the depths of the sea, and the number of the rivers, so that you may see what you are leaving and where you are going.
This will happen after forty days.
Now, therefore, during these days, go and teach the people as much as you can, so that they may learn not to die in the last time, but may learn to live in the last times.”
And I, Baruch, went from there and came to the people. I gathered them, from the greatest to the least, and said to them:
“Listen, children of Israel. See how few of you remain from the twelve tribes of Israel.
Yet to you and your ancestors the Lord gave the law, above all the nations.

And because your brothers transgressed the commandments of the Most High, he brought punishment upon you and upon them. He did not spare the former, but also handed the latter over to captivity, leaving no remnant of them.
And here you are with me.
So if you set your ways straight, you too will not go away as your brothers went away. Instead, they will come to you.
For the one you serve is merciful, and the one in whom you place your hope is compassionate, and he is faithful to do good and not harm.
Have you not yourselves seen what happened to Zion?
Or do you perhaps think that the place sinned and was therefore overthrown, or that the land did something wrong and was therefore handed over?
Do you not know that because of you who sinned, what had not sinned was overthrown, and because of those who acted wickedly, what had done no wrong was handed over to enemies?
And all the people answered me, saying, “As far as we can remember the good things that the Mighty One has done for us, we remember them. And the things we do not remember, he knows in his mercy.
But do this for us, your people: write a letter of instruction and a scroll of hope to our brothers in Babylon as well, so that you may strengthen them too before you leave us.
For Israel’s shepherds have perished, the lamps that used to shine have gone out, and the springs from which we used to drink have stopped flowing.
But we have been left in darkness, in the thicket of the forest, and in the thirst of the wilderness.”
And I answered them, saying, “The shepherds, the lamps, and the springs came from the Law. And though we depart, the Law remains.
If, then, you look to the law and are attentive to wisdom, the lamp will not be lacking, the shepherd will not depart, and the spring will not dry up.

Nevertheless, as you have asked me, I will also write to your brothers in Babylon and send the letter by human messengers. Likewise, I will write to the nine and a half tribes and send the letter by a bird.”
And on the twenty-first day of the eighth month, I, Baruch, came and sat beneath an oak, in the shade of its branches. No one was with me; I was alone.
And I wrote these two letters. One I sent by an eagle to the nine and a half tribes, and the other I sent to those in Babylon by three men.
And I called the eagle and spoke these words to it:
“The Most High made you higher than all the birds.

Now go, and do not stop anywhere. Do not enter a nest or perch on any tree until you have crossed the broad expanse of the great waters of the Euphrates River. Go to the people who live there and drop this letter to them.
Remember that at the time of the flood, Noah received the fruit of an olive tree from a dove after he had sent it out from the ark.
The ravens also served Elijah, bringing him food as they had been commanded.
Solomon too, during his reign, whenever he wanted to send something somewhere or ask for something, would command a bird, and it would obey him, doing as he commanded it.
And now, do not grow weary or turn aside to the right or to the left. Instead, fly and go by a straight path, so that you may keep the command of the Mighty One, as I have told you.”
